The PICOLON experimental room is located at the KamLAND area in Kamioka Underground Laboratory at a depth of 2700 meters water equivalent (m.w.e).
PICOLON plans to build a 250 kg NaI(Tl) experiment in the KamLAND area of the Kamioka Underground Laboratory at a depth of 2,700 m.w.e.

name: PICOLON
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).

Names: the project appears as PICO-LON (2006-2016 papers), KamLAND-PICO (2014 proceedings, arXiv:1407.3542: NaI(Tl) 'installed into KamLAND') and PICOLON (2021 onward); they are treated as one programme by the same group (Tokushima, Tohoku, Osaka RCNP, Kamioka).

Phases: R&D with thin multilayer NaI(Tl) detectors (2006-2007), the first low-background measurement at the Oto Cosmo Observatory (from September 2007), Kamioka measurements from summer 2015; the 250 kg experiment is a plan (arXiv:2607.24448), so the active status covers the small-crystal measurements only.
The Oto Cosmo Observatory placement end (2015) is inferred; see the placement note.
No official PICOLON website was found; PICOLON data and results are in the papers cited.

physics_goals.quote: PICOLON experiment conducts an independent search for Weakly Interacting Massive Particles using highest purity NaI(Tl) crystals.
physics_goals.value: Independent search for WIMPs, and a test of the DAMA/LIBRA annual modulation, with NaI(Tl) crystals of radiopurity comparable to DAMA/LIBRA's

summary.plain: PICOLON is a Japanese search for dark matter with ultra-pure sodium iodide crystals, measured so far with a small crystal deep in the Kamioka mine. It aims to test the yearly signal reported by DAMA/LIBRA with crystals as clean as DAMA's, and plans a 250 kg detector.
summary.technical: Ultra-pure NaI(Tl) crystals made by hybrid purification (recrystallisation plus ion-exchange resins; natural K below 20 ppb, 210Pb below 5.7 uBq/kg), read by a 3-inch low-background Hamamatsu R11065-20 PMT, in a lead and copper shield in the KamLAND area of Kamioka (2700 m.w.e.). Ingot #94 (1.34 kg, ~10 photoelectrons/keV): background ~1.5 /d/kg/keV in 2-6 keVee; first six-month modulation test (2021-2022 data) finds a finite amplitude attributed to non-physical causes. A 250 kg array in the KamLAND area is planned.
